messages:
sara_support: FYI escalated from Acme — they report a big jump in p95/p99 for streaming calls after last runtime deploy. TTFB for first chunk is fine, but total time and chunk spacing are hitting customers. attaching repro steps below.

alex_eng: Can you paste the curl/reqs you're using to reproduce? Also which model + routing config? :eyes:

sara_support: Repro (from their network):

Streaming (good TTFB, chunk gaps):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-x
```

Non-streaming (total time much higher):
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=gpt-x \
  -d '{"prompt":"long prompt...","max_tokens":400}'
```

Note: customer toggled streaming=false to try to mitigate but saw higher p95. They measured p95 jump ~2x for text generation routes.

mike_infra: Do we know whether their requests go through our edge LB -> Akamai -> customer proxy chain? Could be a client-side proxy rebuffering small chunks. Any packet captures?

lina_prod: I grabbed a short tcpdump from a repro run (sensitive — shared in ops ticket). Observed small bursts of ~120-300 bytes with 180ms gaps. Server is emitting smaller chunks after the runtime change that coalesces token frames for cost reasons. Looks like an intermediate proxy is delaying flush for small writes (likely buffering until N bytes or delayed ack timer).

alex_eng: That matches a recent runtime optimization (commit abc123) where we started coalescing sub-token frames to reduce backend CPU/IO. Good for cost but side-effect: fewer, smaller writes that some proxies treat poorly. We intended to gate by a config flag but that slipped through default-on for hosted. :grimacing:

chris_acme: For context from the customer: we see the first chunk in ~60ms, then a 200-400ms pause, then bursts. When we switched to non-streaming the server holds output until completion; surprisingly total latency increased from 850ms to 1.6s p95 (we measured end-to-end). We suspect retries and client timeouts compounding.

sara_support: TL;DR hypothesis: coalescing + client/proxy buffering -> increases inter-chunk gaps; streaming shows TTFB ok but perceivable streaming quality poor; non-streaming increases end-to-end because flush semantics and upstream buffering cause reordering/backpressure.

mike_infra: Quick checks: can the customer try connecting directly to our edge (bypassing their proxy) to confirm? Also check TCP_NODELAY on their side and any nginx/varnish buffer settings. Recommend `curl --no-buffer` and `--http2` to see difference.

lina_prod: Repro command we used internally (streaming vs direct edge):
```
# streaming via edge
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  --http2 https://edge.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-x --no-buffer

# direct to cluster (bypassing LB)
curl -N --resolve "edge.redwood.ai:443:10.1.12.34" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" --http2 --no-buffer https://edge.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-x
```

We saw inter-chunk gaps drop from median ~180ms to ~25ms when hitting the cluster directly.

alex_eng: Immediate mitigation options:
- flip the runtime flag to disable aggressive token coalescing for hosted, revert commit, or enable a per-tenant opt-out (fastest).
- server-side: introduce a flush threshold to ensure we emit a minimum chunk size in first N tokens to avoid proxy buffering.
- client guidance: recommend http2 + --no-buffer and disable client-side proxy buffering.

mike_infra: Ops notes: rollback of the coalescing default is low-risk but may increase cost. We can gate by tenant; for prod customers with SLOs we should default to precise flush. I'll schedule a canary rollback for the next window unless we prefer a config flag toggle (we can flip immediately behind feature flag).

ops-bot: deploy status: last deploy (abc123) to hosted runtime completed 2623451200 by ci-bot. No active rollback in progress.

chris_acme: If you can flip a tenant flag that would be great — our users are sensitive to interactive feel. happy to test.

sara_support: Action items:
- mike_infra: gate rollback behind tenant flag and flip for Acme (ETA 2h) (assigned).
- alex_eng: add server flush threshold patch (small change) + unit test (ETA end of day).
- lina_prod: coordinate direct repro after flip and collect p50/p95/p99 (ETA 1h after change).
- sara_support: keep customer updated, ask them to try direct edge test and send `curl --no-buffer` output.

alex_eng: short-term hotfix PR: set default to `precise_stream_flush=true` for hosted until we have better heuristics. I'll attach PR link in ops ticket. :thumbsup:

mike_infra: Confirmed toggle created: `runtime.streaming.coalesce.enabled = false` for tenant:acme on staging; will promote to prod canary in 30m.

lina_prod: After canary flip to false — internal traces show p95 improved from 1.1s -> 620ms for streaming routes, p99 likewise improved. Will run 50-run batch and post numbers.

chris_acme: Confirmed preliminary tests — feel snappier. Thanks team. Will run overnight load and report if anything else pops up.

sara_support: Closing loop: we'll keep the tenant flag while devs implement a more robust heuristic (min flush bytes + time cap) and publish customer guidance on proxies. Filing follow-up RFC for long-term: leave coalescing but heuristic-aware per upstream path. :white_check_mark:
